method:
ORDER OF JUDGEMENT (Lilly, Christian Astrology 1647, Book III). (1) NATAL PROMISE first: significators of the topic (house, lord, planets in it, Part of Fortune and its lords, natural significator), scored by essential and accidental dignity, judged by plurality of testimonies (p.561; Book I p.101-104, table p.115). (2) ANNUAL PROFECTION second (Chap. CLXVI-CLXXI, p.715-733): lord of the year, judged in the radix and in the revolution; Lilly says profections alone are of little force without directions (p.719), so strength is 2. Bonatti (Pars V p.817-818): profection and revolution are read together. (3) SOLAR RETURN third (p.734-741), cast for the place of residence. (4) TRANSITS last (p.741, day-scale only). Firdaria (Bonatti Pars V p.813-814) is a parallel period-lord. Directions are OUT OF SCOPE. Valens IV.16 agrees that the natal basis limits what a time-lord can do, but that rule was not verified and is held back, so the natal-promise gate is applied only where a rule here states it (none does globally; per critique, gating is a per-rule sourced property, default ungated and shown as such).

DIFFERENCES FROM THE ENGINE: Lilly's terms are Ptolemy's, not the Egyptian bounds in dignities.ts; Lilly gives two triplicity rulers per element (day, night), water is Mars for both, no participating lord; Lilly's 1647 profection moves the Ascendant by degree with two lords in a year when it crosses a sign; Lilly uses Regiomontanus houses while the engine has whole-sign only (rules that cite houses run whole-sign as a labelled variant, or need Regiomontanus cusps).

CHECKER CORRECTIONS APPLIED: classes defined on E alone with A as a flag; wealth-promise rules split and made exclusive (uncovered combinations emit NO signal); duplicate whole-sign year-lord rule dropped (one profected-sign fact, dedupeKey profected-sign:{index}@year); one profection reading per (profected house, topic); 7th removed from asc-hostile; orbs table keeps the primary column only. Page numbers are scan offset (printed = scan leaf minus 33) and chapter numerals come from OCR; Valens read only in Riley's translation, paraphrased.

topicDefinitions.definition: Lilly's 'second house of Riches, or the goods of Fortune': estate, substance, money and how it is gained and kept, judged from the strength of the significators of substance.
topicDefinitions.significators: Cusp of the 2nd house (from 5 degrees before the cusp), the lord of that house, lord of any sign intercepted in it, the Part of Fortune and its lords, Jupiter as general significator of wealth, planets in the 2nd. Lilly p.552 (Chap. CXIII), p.553-563 (Chap. CXIIII-CXVII).
topicDefinitions.source: Lilly 1647, Book III, p.552-563; Ptolemy cited by Lilly at p.552

topicDefinitions.definition: Honour, dignity, preferment and the quality and durability of the Native's public standing and profession.
topicDefinitions.significators: Luminaries (the Sun most considerable) and planets that behold the Lights within the moiety of their orbs; the lord of the mid-heaven; planets in the mid-heaven. Lilly p.615 (Chap. CXLIIII), p.621-626.

topicDefinitions.definition: Marriage and the wife or husband: whether, when, how easily, what kind. Man's significators are Venus and the Moon, then the 7th house and lord; the woman's significators (Sun and Mars) are from damaged OCR and are not used.
topicDefinitions.significators: For a man: Venus and the Moon, the 7th house and its lord, planets in the 7th. Lilly p.587-600 (Chap. CXXX-CXXXVII).

topicDefinitions.definition: Health of body, sickness and its kind (the sixth house).
topicDefinitions.significators: The ascending sign and its lord; Sun and Moon; the 6th house and its lord; planets in the 6th; the 7th house and its lord. Lilly p.576-581.

topicDefinitions.definition: Study, wisdom, science, scholarship. Lilly has no dedicated learning chapter in the pages read; the house table assigns Religion, Wisdom, Science, Learning and Scholarship to the ninth house and Mercury to scholars. Profection houses 9 and 5 carry the only extracted rule.
topicDefinitions.significators: Ninth house and its lord, planets in the 9th, Mercury. Lilly p.557-558, 606-614.
topicDefinitions.source: Lilly 1647, Book III, p.555-558, 606-614; no dedicated chapter found

topicDefinitions.definition: Journeys and residence abroad (ninth house), kindred and short movements (third house), home, lands, patrimony and buildings (fourth house).
topicDefinitions.significators: 9th house and its lord, planets in the 9th, Moon and Mercury; 4th house for home. Lilly p.606-611, 558, 564.

topicDefinitions.definition: The overall fortune of the Native and of the year, from the strength of the Ascendant, its lord, the luminaries and the plurality of planets in essential dignity or debility.
topicDefinitions.significators: All seven planets by essential and accidental fortitude; the Ascendant and its lord; Sun and Moon. Lilly p.551 (Chap. CXIII).

tables.B_accidentalFortitudes: Lilly Book I p.115 table, read from the scan. Fortitudes: in the Midheaven or Ascendant +5; 7th, 4th, 11th +4; 2nd, 5th +3; 9th +2; 3rd +1; direct +4 (void for Sun and Moon); swift +2; Saturn, Jupiter, Mars oriental +2; Venus and Mercury occidental +2; Moon increasing in light or occidental +2; free from combustion and beams +5; cazimi +5; partile conjunction with Jupiter or Venus +5; with the Dragon's Head +4; partile trine to Jupiter or Venus +4; partile sextile to Jupiter or Venus +3; (fixed-star rows Cor Leonis +6, Spica +5 need star data: not computable). Debilities: 12th house -5; 8th and 6th -2; retrograde -5; slow -2; Saturn, Jupiter, Mars occidental -2; Venus and Mercury oriental -2; Moon decreasing -2; combust -5; under the beams -4; partile conjunction with Saturn or Mars -5; with the Dragon's Tail -4; besieged by Saturn and Mars -5; partile opposition to Saturn or Mars -4; partile square -3; (Caput Algol -5 needs star data). Definitions p.112-114: combust within 8 deg 30' of the Sun in the same sign; under the beams to 17 degrees; cazimi within 17 minutes; partile = same degree. The Venus 48 and Mercury 28 maximum elongations were not confirmed (held back).
tables.C_aspectsOrbs: Lilly Book I p.105-107. Aspects: conjunction 0, sextile 60, square 90, trine 120, opposition 180. Orbs of rays (primary column): Saturn 10, Jupiter 12, Mars 7 deg 30', Sun 17, Venus 8, Mercury 7, Moon 12 deg 30'. Platick when distance from the exact aspect is no more than the sum of half of each orb (example Venus and Saturn: 4 + 5 = 9). The 'according to others' column is held back (Mars 7 versus checker's recalled 8, no evidence either way).
tables.D_profectionHouseTable: Lilly Book III Chap. CLXIX p.729-730 (Ascendant and Moon profected through the radical houses): 1 cheerful, provide what the body needs; 2 good to buy and sell, increase of estate; 3 prosper in journeys, converse with kin and religious men; 4 inheritance, new house, blessing from parents, mines, build or repair, but sorrowful and in danger of water, not good for long journeys; 5 pleasure, school or women, good to make covenants, send letters, perfect accounts; 6 sickness, hatred of the vulgar, ill servants, no journeys, ill time to deal in merchandise and contracts; 7 froward, women and wantonness, open enemies, quarrels and suits, good to marry the other significators concurring; 8 body or goods suffer by slander and treachery, no new contracts, not adventurous in trade; 9 long journeys, study and learning, church-men, chemistry; 10 ambition, preferment, eminent men, increase for the tradesman, safe journeys; 11 cheerful, friends increase, very prosperous in worldly affairs; 12 sickly, hidden causes, enmity of ill neighbours, danger of imprisonment or banishment, ill year for great cattle and horses. Table not checked line by line by the checker.
tables.F_firdariaAndTiming: Firdaria (Bonatti Pars V p.813-814): Sun 10, Venus 8, Mercury 13, Moon 9, Saturn 11, Jupiter 12, Mars 7, Head 3, Tail 2 (sum 75); day order Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Head, Tail; the Moon begins at night and the text says 'in all things as is said' for the Sun, but the position of the nodes in the night order and any subdivision of the node periods are NOT in the lines read, so they follow the engine's named firdariaNodes convention; sub-lords by sevenths in the order Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars starting at the major lord. Profection timing (Lilly p.715-727): 30 degrees per year, about 12.17 days per degree (365.2422/30); round days to the nearest day (Lilly's example prints 284 for 23 deg 23 min; exact is about 284.7).

rules.name: Planetary strength classes from Lilly's dignity scores
rules.condition: For each planet compute E (essential score, Table A, sect-aware triplicity) and A (accidental score, Table B). CLASS IS DEFINED ON E ALONE (derived, not Lilly's wording): STRONG if E >= +3; MODERATE if E is +1 or +2; WEAK if E < 0. A is carried as a separate flag 'afflicted' if A <= -5, so a planet is never in two classes. Thresholds 3 and -5 are the implementer's operationalisation of Lilly's words; his numbers are in the tables. 'Benevolent significator' (p.560) = Jupiter, Venus, or any planet standing in the dignities of a good planet.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book I Chap. XVIII p.101-104 and table p.115; Book III Chap. CXVI p.560
rules.sourceLocator: Book I p.101-104, 115; Book III p.560
rules.variants: Egyptian bounds (engine now) and Dorothean three-ruler triplicities give different E values. Later writers let reception change a planet's class; Lilly counts mutual reception by house as 5 and by exaltation as 4 (p.115). The earlier quote 'we allow for that five dignities' was a fragment that does not support the classes and is removed.
rules.verificationNote: Class on E only, A as flag; thresholds labelled derived; unsupported quote removed.

rules.name: Wealth promise: significators of substance strong
rules.condition: S_w = {domicile lord of the 2nd cusp sign; each planet in the 2nd (house from 5 degrees before the 2nd cusp to 5 degrees before the 3rd, or whole-sign variant); domicile lord of the sign holding the Part of Fortune; Jupiter}. Classes by E only. Part of Fortune = Asc + Moon - Sun by day, Asc + Sun - Moon by night. Outcomes: (i) at least half of S_w STRONG and at least half of S_w in angles (1, 4, 7, 10): 'a very great Estate, plenty of all things'; (ii) STRONG outnumber WEAK but (i) fails: comfortable estate by the number of fortitudes. 'At least half' and the (ii) wording are derived thresholds. Combinations not covered by the strong, weak and mixed wealth rules emit NO signal.
rules.template: The significators of wealth ({list}) are strong, with {n_angular} angular: the nativity promises a {level} estate.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CXIII-CXIIII; after Ptolemy Tetrabiblos IV.1 and Leovitius, Origanus as cited by Lilly
rules.sourceLocator: Book III p.552-554 (Chap. CXIIII 'Whether the Native shall be Rich')
rules.variants: Lilly follows Leovitius and Origanus and says Ptolemy is 'extreame short' (p.553). 'Lords of the Part of Fortune' may include the exaltation lord; the engine uses the domicile lord first. Whether the significators are fortunes or infortunes does not matter, only strength (p.553). Regiomontanus versus whole-sign houses change which planets count as in the 2nd. The quote used by the researcher supported the weak case, not this one, so none is shown.
rules.verificationNote: Thresholds labelled derived; classes by E only; unrelated quote removed; fall-through emits no signal.

rules.name: Wealth promise: all significators of substance weak
rules.condition: With S_w as in lilly.wealth.promise-strong: every member of S_w is WEAK (E < 0). Verdict: poverty or great want.
rules.template: All significators of wealth ({list}) are weak: the nativity promises want.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CXIIII 'Signes of Poverty'
rules.sourceQuote: all the Significators weak, argue poverty
rules.variants: Same as lilly.wealth.promise-strong. The three branches were one rule in the source; the page locator is shared and a separate locator per branch was not recorded.
rules.verificationNote: Split from the original weak rule so each branch has its own id.

rules.name: Wealth promise: most significators weak, Fortunes cadent, Infortunes angular
rules.condition: More than half of S_w are WEAK and the Fortunes (Jupiter, Venus) are in cadent houses (3, 6, 9, 12) while the Infortunes (Saturn, Mars) are angular. Verdict: poverty or great want.
rules.template: Most significators of wealth are weak, the Fortunes cadent and the Infortunes angular: want is promised.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CXIIII 'Signes of Poverty'
rules.verificationNote: Split; no quote seen for this branch.

rules.name: Wealth promise: Moon combust with an unfortunate dispositor, or the Part of Fortune oppressed
rules.condition: The Moon is combust and her dispositor is an unfortunate planet (Saturn or Mars), OR the Part of Fortune (or its lord) is oppressed by the infortunes and cadent. Verdict: from a vast estate the Native comes to great want.
rules.template: The Moon is combust and her dispositor {planet} is unfortunate (or the Part of Fortune is oppressed): loss of estate is promised.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CXIIII 'Signes of Poverty'
rules.variants: Lilly writes further aphorisms in the same passage; only the generic ones are kept.
rules.verificationNote: Split; no quote seen for this branch.

rules.name: Lord of the year from the profected Ascendant (Lilly by-degree; two lords when the sign changes)
rules.condition: Lilly's 1647 method moves the Ascendant 30 degrees per solar year: profected Ascendant at t = natal Ascendant + 30 * (years elapsed since birth, fractional); the year runs from solar return to solar return. Lord of the year = domicile lord of the sign of the profected Ascendant. If the profected Ascendant crosses into the next sign during the year, two lords: the first for the days it takes to reach the boundary (about 12.17 days per degree, rounded to the nearest day), then the lord of the next sign. The whole-sign variant (one lord per year by age mod 12) is NOT a separate rule here: it is the same fact as valens.profection.transmission-lord and runs there only.
rules.template: Annual profection to {sign}: Lord of the year {lord} until {date}, then {lord2}.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXVI-CLXVIII 'Of annuall Profections'; 'How to judge upon a Figure of Projections'
rules.sourceLocator: Book III p.715-716 (Chap. CLXVI), p.719-720 (Chap. CLXVII), p.727 (Chap. CLXVIII)
rules.sourceQuote: the Lord of the yeer, who is ever that Planet that is Lord of the Signe ascending in the Profection
rules.variants: Whole-sign profection (Valens IV.11, Bonatti p.817) keeps the same degree in each new sign. Bonatti (p.818) gives days by multiplying degrees to the next sign by 12 and one sixth. Lilly calls monthly and daily profections more scrupulous than necessary (p.716).
rules.verificationNote: Two methods under one id separated; whole-sign duplicate dropped; days rounded.

rules.name: Profected Ascendant in the radical 2nd, 4th, 10th or 11th house (money)
rules.condition: Profected Ascendant sign in radical house h counted by whole sign from the natal Ascendant sign: h = (profected sign index - natal Ascendant sign index) mod 12 + 1. Direction PER HOUSE: h=2 favourable (good to buy and sell, increase of estate); h=10 favourable (preferment, increase for the tradesman); h=11 favourable (very prosperous in worldly affairs); h=4 MIXED (inheritance, a new house, blessing from parents, but sorrowful, not good for long journeys). Emit one reading per (profected house, topic) from Table D; cross-references to other houses are not re-emitted. Lilly: profections of themselves without Directions are not of much validity, so strength is one notch below a natal promise.
rules.template: Profected Ascendant stands in the {h}th house ({sign}): a year favourable for {matter}.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXIX 'Of the Profections of the Ascendant and Moon, and what they signifie in every House'; Chap. CLXVII p.719
rules.sourceLocator: Book III p.729-730 (Chap. CLXIX); p.719 (Chap. CLXVII)
rules.sourceQuote: Profections of themselves without Directions are not of much validity
rules.variants: Lilly's title refers to the Ascendant and the Moon profected through the houses; the Moon's profection is read from the same table. Whole-sign counting differs from Lilly's by-degree houses (Regiomontanus).
rules.verificationNote: Direction made per house; house 4 mixed; one reading per (house, topic).

rules.name: Profected Ascendant in the radical 7th or 5th house (marriage and love)
rules.condition: Profected Ascendant in radical house 7: inclined to women and wantonness, many open enemies, quarrels and lawsuits; 'good to marry, the other Significators concurring'. In house 5: pleasure according to his age, good for covenants, letters and accounts. Houses 8 and 12 are the cross-reference to the house-loss reading and are NOT emitted again here. One reading per (profected house, topic).
rules.template: Profected Ascendant stands in the {h}th house: marriage, love and open enmity are the year's themes.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXIX
rules.variants: Direction is 'activates' because the same year carries a good time to marry and quarrels.
rules.verificationNote: Duplicate 8th/12th sentence removed to avoid double counting.

rules.name: Profected Ascendant in the radical 9th or 5th house (study)
rules.condition: Profected Ascendant in radical house 9: a convenient time for study and learning, familiar with church-men. In house 5: at school with his equals. One reading per (profected house, topic).
rules.template: Profected Ascendant stands in the {h}th house: a year for study.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXIX
rules.variants: Split out of the original learning-and-travel rule.

rules.name: Profected Ascendant in the radical 9th, 3rd or 4th house (journeys)
rules.condition: House 9: a convenient time for long journeys (favourable). House 3: prosper in journeys, converse with kindred (favourable). House 4: not good to go long journeys, danger in water (caution, MIXED, shown as a caution note). One reading per (profected house, topic).
rules.template: Profected Ascendant stands in the {h}th house: a year for {journeys}.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXIX
rules.variants: The house-4 warning contradicts a travel-favourable reading; shown as a cautionary note.

rules.name: Valens: the year transmits from the Ascendant, Sun and Moon by counting signs by age
rules.condition: For the current year number N = age in completed years + 1, r = N mod 12 (12 when 0). From each of Ascendant, Sun, Moon count r signs inclusively: the receiving sign is (r - 1) signs after the starting sign (whole-sign profection, age mod 12). RECEIVER = the domicile lord of the receiving sign; each planet standing in that sign is a further, separate transmission. Worked check from Valens: the 35th year gives remainder 11 and counts from Virgo to Cancer. The pair verdict (Table E) and the benefic-count verdict are HELD BACK (unverified), so this rule emits 'activates' with the transmitter and receiver named, never a favourable or unfavourable verdict. This is the single whole-sign year-lord rule (Lilly whole-sign variant removed as a duplicate).
rules.sourceCitation: Vettius Valens, Anthologies Book IV ch. 11 'The operative year and the method of fractions', tr. Mark T. Riley (archive.org edition of 2019)
rules.sourceLocator: Book IV ch. 11, Riley p.102-103 (the paragraph beginning 'when investigating the current year of a nativity')
rules.variants: Valens also tabulates from Lots for critical illnesses, benefactions and dangers, counts from the four angles in the 'more scientific' method, and in IV.27 reports Seuthos's school starting from Sun, Moon, Ascendant or Lot of Fortune by sect.
rules.verificationNote: Receiver defined; verdict part held back with the unverified pair table.

rules.name: Firdaria: the period lord and sub-lord are judged by their natal condition
rules.condition: Major periods (Table F): Sun 10, Venus 8, Mercury 13, Moon 9, Saturn 11, Jupiter 12, Mars 7, North Node 3, South Node 2 (sum 75). Day birth begins with the Sun in the order Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Head, Tail, then the Sun. Night birth begins with the Moon, 'in all things as is said' for the Sun: the order of the nodes in the night cycle and the absence of node sub-periods follow the engine's named firdariaNodes convention and are printed with every result. Each planetary major period is divided in seven equal parts starting with the major lord then the others in the order Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars. Judgement: 'all these significators or disposers' act according to their condition: well disposed they increase fortunes and decrease misfortunes; badly disposed the reverse. Compute class (strength classes) and house for the major lord and the sub-lord; topics follow the houses the lord rules and occupies.
inputs: houses ruled and occupied by lord
rules.template: Firdaria: major lord {major}, sub-lord {minor} until {date}; major lord is {class}: indications for {topics} are {verdict}.
rules.sourceCitation: Guido Bonatti, De astronomia tractatus X (Basel, 1550), Pars V, Caput III 'De annis Firdariae et ipsorum dispositionibus', Google-digitised copy on archive.org (bub_gb_BgWuc5O-JzIC)
rules.sourceLocator: Pars V p.813-814 (scan leaf n415-416); the night-birth order and the position of the nodes within it are on p.814 and are not stated in the lines read
rules.sourceQuote: Nam si natiuitas fuerit diurna, incipiet a Sole, quod est luminare diurnum
rules.variants: Lilly (1647, p.733-734) gives a different septennial scheme (read from OCR, not verified): held back. The checker recalls the usual night order Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Head, Tail, Sun, Venus, Mercury (unsourced memory, recorded as a candidate for firdariaNodes only). Attribution to Abu Ma'shar was not seen.
rules.verificationNote: Night order and node handling made an explicit named convention.

rules.name: Revolution: return Ascendant square or opposite the natal Ascendant, or in the signs of the bad radical houses 6 and 12
rules.condition: Cast the solar return at the place of residence. Fires if the return Ascendant sign is square the natal Ascendant sign, or is the natal 6th or 12th house sign (the natal 7th, opposition, is NOT tested here: it belongs to lilly.revolution.seventh-asc, held back, and is omitted to avoid overlap, so opposition alone does not fire this rule). Verdict: loss and detriment that year according to the nature of the radical house that sign was; fear sickness and bodily weakness, especially if those houses were unfortunate in the radix.
rules.template: The return Ascendant falls in the natal {h}th house sign: the year carries the troubles of that house.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXXII 'Of Revolutions'
rules.variants: The returns of an infortune to its radical place (peril that year) are the separate lilly.revolution.returns-affliction rule, held back.

rules.name: Transit by day over the radical Ascendant, Midheaven and radical planets (Lilly)
rules.condition: Restricted to points the engine has: the natal Ascendant and Midheaven degrees and radical planet longitudes (cusps of the 2nd and 3rd house need Regiomontanus cusps and are not used). Transits found from an ephemeris: the day a planet passes the point or beholds it by sextile, square, trine or conjunction. Jupiter or Venus over the ascending degree: a healthful, cheerful, successful day; Mars over it: choler or passion for two or three days; Saturn: gravity, melancholy. Fortunate days: Jupiter, Venus, Sun or Moon in sextile or trine to the ascending or culminating degree or their own radical places. Unsuccessful days: Saturn or Mars over the ascending or culminating degrees or the radical places of Jupiter, Venus, Sun or Moon, or beholding them. Point orb is the transiting planet's half-orb (Table C): a derived choice, Lilly gives none.
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book III Chap. CLXXIIII 'Of the Transit of the Planets'
rules.sourceQuote: The Transit of the Planets is best found out by an Ephemeris
rules.variants: Lilly treats transits as day-scale only; he gives no year-scale rules for Jupiter and Saturn. The glyph list of fortunate days is OCR-damaged and read as Jupiter, Venus, Sun, Moon.
rules.verificationNote: Restricted to computable points; the 2nd-cusp 'money day' clause removed; topic general only.

rules.name: Jupiter transiting the year sign or its square and opposite points
rules.condition: The year sign is the PROFECTED SIGN (the receiving sign of the whole-sign profection), not the sign where its lord stands. If transiting Jupiter stands in the year sign or in a sign square or opposite it: with the time-lord well situated or in operative places (angles), great public services and high rank; with the time-lord unfavourably situated, delay and unsettledness. The 'Jupiter rising' modifier is dropped (no sourced elongation threshold). 'In any nativity Jupiter has an extraordinary effect.'
inputs: class of lord of the year
rules.template: Transiting Jupiter stands in {sign}, {relation} to the year sign {year_sign}: {verdict} for rank and public service.
rules.sourceCitation: Vettius Valens, Anthologies Book IV ch. 14 'The phases and transits of the stars', tr. Mark T. Riley
rules.sourceLocator: Book IV ch. 14, Riley p.107 (archive.org text lines 9082-9145)
rules.variants: Houses are whole-sign (Valens' Places). Valens' 'rising' means heliacal visibility phases (dropped here).
rules.verificationNote: Year sign defined as the profected sign; rising dropped.

rules.name: Critical year: the year sign is the prenatal syzygy sign, its square or opposite, with Saturn in a cadent sign
rules.condition: The profected year sign (counting years from the Ascendant sign) is the sign of the new or full Moon before birth, or the sign square or opposite it, AND Saturn is transiting one of the four signs that just precede the angles at the nativity (whole-sign houses 12, 3, 6, 9 from the Ascendant sign). Verdict (with the natal basis in accord): crisis of health; sometimes livelihood and rank if benefics do not aspect the body. The 'Saturn at its natal distance from the ruler of the prenatal syzygy' clause is dropped (not programmable as written).
rules.template: Year {N} is in the sign of the prenatal {new or full} Moon or its square or opposition, and Saturn is in {sign}: a critical year for health.
rules.sourceCitation: Vettius Valens, Anthologies Book V ch. 2 'The critical year. The ecliptic places. Initiatives', tr. Mark T. Riley
rules.sourceLocator: Book V ch. 2, Riley p.124-125 (archive.org text lines 10582-10640)
rules.variants: Nothing in the opened texts states a verdict for an eclipse on a natal point. Output wording is 'health caution' only; no mortality statement.
rules.verificationNote: Split into syzygy and node parts; unprogrammable clause dropped.

rules.name: Critical period: Saturn at or square the lunar node
rules.condition: Transiting Saturn conjunct or opposite the mean node (Valens' 'ecliptic places') or at the points square to them. Same-degree match is stronger and a same-sign match weaker and delayed; no orb is set by the text, so the engine uses same-sign as the weak form and 1 degree as the strong form (derived).
rules.template: Saturn stands at the {node} or its square ({degreeMatch}): a critical period for health.
rules.sourceCitation: Vettius Valens, Anthologies Book V ch. 2, tr. Mark T. Riley
rules.sourceLocator: Book V ch. 2, Riley p.124-125 (archive.org text lines 10582-10640)
rules.variants: Valens' 'ecliptic places' are the lunar nodes; the engine uses the mean node.
rules.verificationNote: Split out of the original critical-year rule.

rules.name: Aspects and orbs as Lilly gives them
rules.condition: Five aspects only: conjunction (0), sextile (60), square (90), trine (120), opposition (180). Sextile and trine friendly (trine more forcibly), square imperfect enmity, opposition perfect hatred, conjunction good or bad as the planets are friends or enemies. Partile = same degree; platick = within the sum of the two planets' moieties. Orbs (primary column only, Table C): Saturn 10, Jupiter 12, Mars 7 30', Sun 17, Venus 8, Mercury 7, Moon 12 30'. Combustion within 8 deg 30' of the Sun in the same sign; under the beams to 17 degrees; cazimi within 17 minutes. Oriental superior planets between conjunction and opposition. Besieged between Saturn and Mars. The alternative orb column and the maximum elongations of Venus and Mercury are held back (unconfirmed).
rules.sourceCitation: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (London, 1647), Book I Chap. XIX; table of orbs on p.107; combustion p.113-114
rules.sourceQuote: they stand thus as I have found by the best Authors and my owne Experience
rules.variants: Sun's orb 17 or 15, Moon 12.5 or 12 by author; for planet-to-point Lilly gives no separate orb.
rules.verificationNote: Disputed alternative column and elongations removed.
